title: From learning to earning: an AI career coach for students choosing what comes next
gist: World Bank economists report preliminary results from a pre-registered randomized trial of 'Eligiendo Mi Camino', an LLM-based AI career coach deployed in over 100 Peruvian public schools with Lima's DRELM, startups uDocz and Aidea, and Anthropic. At roughly $0.24 per student per month it delivers personalized counseling that previously cost professional time, moving career-readiness up 0.12 SD and raising intentions to enroll in technical institutes by 14%, with connectivity — not cost — identified as the binding constraint on scale.

themes.theme: The school-to-work transition as a development bottleneck

insights.claim: Over the next decade 1.2 billion young people in developing countries will reach working age, making the quality of their school-to-work transition a first-order macro variable.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: The scale of the incoming cohort means any cheap, replicable intervention on labor-market matching has enormous aggregate leverage on emerging-market productivity.
insights.quote: Over the next decade, 1.2 billion young people in developing countries will reach working age.
insights.locator: Over the next decade, 1.2 billion young people

insights.claim: In a Lima public school classroom, a teacher counted only five or six students out of 27 who knew what they wanted to study.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Roughly 80% of final-year students entering the labor market with no plan is a concrete measure of the human-capital allocation failure this intervention targets.
insights.locator: Ask a Lima public school classroom who knows what they want to study

insights.claim: Peru folds career guidance into a weekly tutoring hour led by classroom teachers rather than dedicated counselors, part of what the OECD calls 'patchy' school career guidance across Latin America.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: The absence of a professional counseling workforce means there is no incumbent to displace — AI enters a vacuum rather than competing with existing staff.
insights.quote: part of what the OECD describes as "patchy" school career guidance across Latin America
insights.locator: in Peru, career guidance is folded into a weekly tutoring hour

insights.claim: First-generation higher-education candidates cannot get guidance from the people they trust most because their families have never navigated those paths.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Information poverty is socially inherited, so interventions that bypass family networks entirely have outsized effect on the marginal student.
insights.locator: Many would be the first in their families to reach higher education

themes.theme: Why information campaigns failed and personalization is the active ingredient

insights.claim: Students systematically misjudge the returns to education, and correcting those beliefs can shift behavior, per Jensen 2010 and Hastings, Neilson and Zimmerman 2015.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Belief correction is an established causal channel, so measured belief shifts are a legitimate leading indicator for eventual enrollment behavior.
insights.locator: Economists have tried to fill the gap with information

insights.claim: Generic information campaigns have mixed results because information arrives generic while the students' questions are personal — which careers fit her interests, what they pay and cost, and what her first step should be.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Explains why a decade of cheap information interventions underdelivered and why personalization, not content, is where the value sits.
insights.quote: information alone has had mixed results, likely because information arrives generic while the questions are personal
insights.locator: But information alone has had mixed results

insights.claim: Intensive mentoring changes student decisions where information provision and even cash incentives do not, but personal guidance is costly to scale and effectively reaches only families who can pay.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Identifies the exact economic gap — high-efficacy, high-cost service rationed by income — that cheap AI inference is positioned to arbitrage.
insights.quote: intensive mentoring works where information and even cash incentives do not
insights.locator: What moves decisions is personal

insights.claim: The expensive part of career counseling was never the information but the professional's time to personalize it, and that is precisely the input AI now substitutes for.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A generalizable rule for identifying which services AI disrupts first: those where cost is dominated by human personalization time rather than content creation.
insights.quote: What was expensive about counseling was never the information; it was the professional’s time to personalize it.
insights.locator: What was expensive about counseling

insights.claim: Eligiendo Mi Camino was built with Lima's regional education authority DRELM, Peruvian startups uDocz and Aidea, and AI lab Anthropic, and pairs an AI career coach with an AI math tutor.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Frontier AI labs are now embedded directly in sovereign public-education delivery in emerging markets, a distribution channel worth tracking for model vendors.
insights.locator: The AI career coach is one of two components

insights.claim: The AI coach costs about 0.24 dollars per student per month, roughly one dollar per student for the four-month program beyond fixed setup costs.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Sub-dollar per-student pricing puts personalized guidance inside any education ministry budget line, which is the whole scaling argument.
insights.quote: at about 0.24 dollars per student per month, roughly one dollar per student for the four-month program beyond fixed setup costs
insights.locator: That is the part AI now covers

insights.claim: The deployment required no new staff, no new devices and no extra instructional time — it ran in existing school computer labs during the school day with teachers given two days of training.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Zero incremental capex and headcount is why this can scale nationally without a budget appropriation fight — the key differentiator from ed-tech hardware programs.
insights.quote: No new staff, no new devices, no extra instructional time.
insights.locator: In Lima the coach ran inside the school day

insights.claim: The eight-step student journey is organized around three questions — who am I, what are my real options, and what is my concrete plan — and draws on salary data for more than 130 occupations across twelve sectors.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: The system's edge comes from local labor-market salary data, meaning the moat is the dataset and localization, not the model.
insights.locator: Since April and running through July

insights.claim: The AI coach interviews students about interests and doubts, corrects the myths they hold, and lets them rehearse the conversation with family because family expectations can be the hardest obstacle.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Treating family negotiation as an explicit design surface is a non-obvious product insight for consumer AI in emerging markets.
insights.locator: In addition, the AI coach interviews each student

insights.claim: The program is being evaluated in a pre-registered randomized trial across more than 100 public schools and over 4,500 students, described as among the first randomized evaluations of an LLM-based career coach in a developing country.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Rigorous RCT evidence on LLM deployment in public services is scarce; results here will anchor procurement decisions across other ministries.
insights.quote: to our knowledge, it is among the first randomized evaluations of an LLM-based career coach in a developing country
insights.locator: We evaluate the program in a pre-registered randomized trial

insights.claim: Nearly nine in ten treated students are actively using the AI platform, an unusually high take-up rate for a school-based digital intervention.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: High take-up removes the usual failure mode of ed-tech pilots and suggests engagement, not adoption, is the solved part of the problem.
insights.quote: Nearly nine in ten treated students are using the platform.
insights.locator: Take-up is high

insights.claim: Treated students score 0.12 standard deviations higher on a five-measure career-readiness index covering certainty, information, feasibility, sector knowledge and self-knowledge.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A 0.12 SD effect at roughly one dollar per student is an extreme cost-effectiveness ratio by education-intervention standards.
insights.locator: Treated students score 0.12 standard deviations higher

insights.claim: Control students estimate a two-year technical degree pays about S/1,300 a month against the roughly S/1,922 that technically educated workers actually earn according to INEI, a gap of nearly one third.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Systematic undervaluation of vocational returns depresses supply into exactly the technical occupations emerging-market employers cannot fill.
insights.locator: control students estimate a two-year technical degree pays about S/1,300

insights.claim: The AI coach moves treated students' salary estimates for technical education up by roughly 21 percent toward the true value, and intentions to enroll in a technical institute rise by 14 percent.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: If intentions convert, this is a cheap lever to redirect youth toward short-cycle vocational tracks that regional labor markets actually reward.
insights.quote: intentions to enroll in a technical institute rise by 14 percent
insights.locator: The coach moves treated students’ estimates up by roughly 21 percent

insights.claim: The reported outcomes are beliefs and plans, not yet realized enrollment decisions, and the program is still ongoing.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: The authors explicitly flag the intention-to-action gap — do not underwrite enrollment effects on this evidence alone.
insights.quote: These are beliefs and plans, not yet enrollment decisions.
insights.locator: Plans follow beliefs

themes.theme: Connectivity, not cost, is the scaling constraint

insights.claim: Because the guidance is data-based, the platform travels to any labor market simply by loading local salaries and options.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Low localization cost means the addressable market is every education ministry with wage microdata, not just Peru.
insights.quote: load local salaries and options and it works in any labor market
insights.locator: At a dollar per student, the program fits any ministry budget

insights.claim: The binding constraint on scaling the AI career coach is connectivity rather than budget, because the coach runs on a cloud-based model and internet access is far from universal.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Reframes the emerging-market AI bottleneck from inference cost to network infrastructure — bullish for edge/on-device inference and rural connectivity buildouts.
insights.quote: The binding constraint for scale is connectivity
insights.locator: The binding constraint for scale is connectivity

insights.claim: The team is exploring a small language model that runs locally without internet access to overcome the connectivity constraint.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Public-sector demand in low-connectivity geographies is a concrete commercial driver for small on-device models, distinct from consumer privacy use cases.
insights.quote: So we are exploring a small language model that runs locally, without internet.
insights.locator: But the coach runs on a cloud-based model

insights.claim: Peru is waiting on the evaluation results to decide on national scale-up while Ecuador is already adapting the platform.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Cross-border adoption before final results indicates political demand is running ahead of the evidence — expect fast regional replication.
insights.quote: Peru is waiting on this evaluation to decide on scale; Ecuador is adapting the platform.
insights.locator: Peru is waiting on this evaluation to decide on scale

insights.claim: The World Bank's jobs agenda asks education systems to deliver better school-to-work transitions rather than only better test scores, especially for young people the labor market currently skips.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Signals a measurable reweighting of World Bank education lending toward employment outcomes over learning assessments.
insights.locator: That is what the World Bank’s jobs agenda asks of education systems
